graphMathHelp.title: How the graph thinks
graphMathHelp.subtitle: Every number on a node comes from a formula. Here's each one.
graphMathHelp.ownExplanation3: . A finished hard task contributes more to a goal's percentage than a finished easy one. If a goal has no tasks, its
graphMathHelp.ownExplanation5: progress is 0 by definition — completion has to come from somewhere upstream.
graphMathHelp.ownExample: Three tasks: difficulty 1 (done), 2 (done), 3 (not done). Total weight = 6, completed weight = 3.
graphMathHelp.depsExplanation1: An incoming connection means "this goal's success depends on that one's." Edge weights say
graphMathHelp.depsExplanation3: . Dependency progress is the weighted average of every predecessor's
graphMathHelp.depsExplanation5: (so the calculation cascades all the way back through the graph).
graphMathHelp.depsExample: Goal A depends on B (weight 70, 80% complete) and C (weight 30, 50% complete).
graphMathHelp.totalFormula:
with own tasks:    total = own × 0.40 + deps × 0.60
without own tasks: total = own × 0.10 + deps × 0.90
graphMathHelp.totalExplanation1: When a goal has its own tasks, both numbers count — but dependencies still get the heavier vote (60%) because work doesn't happen in isolation. When a goal has
graphMathHelp.totalExplanation3: (a pure orchestration node, e.g., "Stay healthy"), it leans almost entirely on its dependencies. The clamp at the end keeps the result inside [0, 100].
graphMathHelp.importanceFormula:
avg = Σ(outgoingEdge.weight) / count(outgoingEdges)

Low      if no outgoing edges, OR avg ≤ 33.3
Medium   if 33.3 < avg < 66.6
High     if avg ≥ 66.6
graphMathHelp.importanceExplanation1: A goal's importance is read from how heavily
graphMathHelp.importanceExplanation3: . A goal with strong outgoing edges (averaging high weight) is a load-bearing column in your structure. A goal nothing depends on is just a leaf.
graphMathHelp.miniMapFormula:
red    if total < 33%
yellow if 33% ≤ total < 67%
green  if total ≥ 67%
graphMathHelp.miniMapExplanation1: The minimap in the bottom-right shades each node by its
graphMathHelp.miniMapExplanation3: so you can scan the whole graph at once and see where the cold spots are.
graphMathHelp.rationaleIntro: The graph treats goals as a network, not a list. Two ideas drive every formula above:
graphMathHelp.rationaleConnectionsBody: An edge says "this feeds that." Importance and dependency progress both fall out of the same edges; you only have to maintain one piece of structure.
graphMathHelp.rationaleDifficultyBody: Counting completed tasks alone treats a 10-minute errand the same as a multi-week project. Weighting by difficulty makes percentages mean something closer to actual effort.

self.attachmentSubtitle: What I want, and fear, when I'm close to someone.
self.loveGiveSubtitle: How I show care. Often diverges from how I best receive it.
self.loveReceiveSubtitle: What actually lands as love when someone offers it.
self.apologySubtitle: What I need to hear after harm — and what I default to giving.
self.conflictSubtitle: The mode I drop into when something goes sideways.
self.stressSubtitle: What my body does when I'm overloaded. Attachment is what I want; this is what I do.
self.releasedHelper: Releases, not regrets: stories, roles and expectations I no longer carry.
self.yearAheadTitle: What I want to be different in a year
self.yearAheadHelper: Concrete and observable. Not "be more confident" — "say no without explaining why."
self.futureHelper: What you'd want them to know. Read this when you've forgotten.
self.attachmentSecureDesc: Comfortable with closeness and with distance. Trusts that needs can be expressed and met. Repairs after conflict. Can be alone without anxiety.
self.attachmentAnxiousDesc: Wants closeness, fears abandonment. Reads neutral signals as rejection. Pursues when a partner pulls away. Self-worth feels tied to the relationship's state.
self.attachmentAvoidantDesc: Values independence, uncomfortable with too much closeness. Pulls back when things get intense. Deactivates emotions; focuses on a partner's flaws when feeling vulnerable.
self.attachmentDisorganizedDesc: Wants closeness and fears it. Push-pull. Often comes from inconsistent or frightening early caregiving. Come here / go away.
self.loveActsDesc: Doing things — errands, fixing, lightening the load.
self.loveGiftsDesc: Tangible tokens of being thought of.
self.loveTouchDesc: Hugs, hand-holding, sitting close. Non-sexual touch counts most.
self.apologyRegretDesc: “I'm sorry I hurt you.” Naming the impact.
self.apologyResponsibilityDesc: “I was wrong.” No deflection, no excuses.
self.apologyRestitutionDesc: “How can I make this right?” Repair the harm.
self.apologyRepentingDesc: “I'll do this differently.” Naming the change.
self.apologyForgivenessDesc: “Will you forgive me?” Asking, not assuming.
self.conflictCompetingDesc: High assertiveness, low cooperation. Win the argument.
self.conflictAvoidingDesc: Low both. Step away and hope it dissolves.
self.conflictAccommodatingDesc: Low assertiveness, high cooperation. Yield to keep peace.
self.conflictCompromisingDesc: Middle on both. Each gives some; neither fully satisfied.
self.conflictCollaboratingDesc: High both. Widen the solution so both needs get met.
self.stressFawnDesc: Appease, caretake, suppress your own needs to keep the peace.

hero.eyebrow: The place to talk about your life · with yourself first

hero.body: Goals that know which values they answer to. People you tend to, not manage. Reflections that compound, week after week. One thinking surface for the long arc of a life.

manifesto.chapter: Chapter I · the shape of it
manifesto.intro: Every app built around “your goals” eventually becomes a guilt machine. anansi bets the other way: the things worth tending are too slow for streaks.
isnt: A journal you forget to write in
No streaks, no badges, no nudges.
manifesto.isBody1: A place to write down what you want and notice which threads pull at which. A reflection-only Personal CRM that asks not “when did I last contact them” but “what do I want to repair?” A Self page that's a portrait.
manifesto.isBody2: Empty fields read as clean pages. The system computes which goal is now important from the threads you've drawn. Tasks promote themselves toward you as their deadline approaches.
manifesto.isBody3: anansi is what you'd build for yourself if you trusted slow software.

surfaces.title: Six places to put a thought.
surfaces.intro: Each one has a different shape because the kinds of thinking it holds are different. A goal, a person, a value and a weekly note each want their own.

pulse.name: Pulse
pulse.body: What's the week asking of you, right now. Tracking items to fill in. Upcoming bids to make. Next month's horizon, quietly visible underneath.

self.name: Self
self.body: This-year shape. My story. How I love, apologize, fight, stress. The patterns I'm catching gently. Released. Just for me. A page you write for yourself.

objectives.name: Objectives
objectives.cap: a graph of what you want, weighted
objectives.body: Goals as cards on a free-positioned canvas. Connections carry weight. Importance is computed, not declared. Look at the canvas and the heaviness shows you where to look.

people.name: People
people.body: No phone numbers, no last-contacted timer. Per person: appreciation, my needs, legacy message, next bids, the dates that matter. To-process · exploring · long-term · context-bound.

values.name: Values
values.body: Named, colored tags that ride along with goals. Each value carries its own behavior list — short evidence sentences for what living this value looks like, this week.

bucket.name: Bucket List
bucket.cap: the things to do before dying
bucket.body: Tag each item with the people you want to do it with. A list of moments you'd grieve not having tried.

whispers.intro: anansi holds the things you don't say out loud. So when people talk about it, they tend to whisper. We asked. Here's what they wrote back — anonymous, as they wanted.
whispers.disclaimer: We don't publish identifying details. anansi is the kind of software where most users would rather not be named — and we'd rather earn quiet trust than loud reach.

designer.body: It's the first place I've written anything down where I don't feel watched by a streak. I missed three weeks and it didn't punish me. I came back because I wanted to.

engineer.body: I used the People section to write down what I needed from my brother for ten years. We had the conversation a month later. He cried. I didn't know I knew it that clearly until it was on the page.

therapist.body: It is the only app I've ever used that doesn't make me feel slightly worse about myself when I open it. I open it more.

founder.body: My goals don't feel like a checklist anymore. They feel like questions I'm asking myself. The weight thing — where importance is just visible — changed how I think about ambition.

writer.body: The Self page is something I'd never have written by myself. The prompts are gentle. “How do I apologize.” “How I love when I love well.” I'd never have asked. I'm glad someone did.

director.body: I run a 40-person team. anansi is the only software I have that's just for me. That distinction matters more than I expected.

claude.intro: anansi speaks Model Context Protocol. Connect it to Claude — Desktop, Code, or claude.ai — and capture goals, schedule next bids, edit your Self page, all by talking.
examples: Schedule coffee with Mom next Tuesday.
Add 'apologize to Lucia' as a next bid, due in two weeks.
What's on my mind for the year ahead?
Create a goal for the marathon and tag it with health and growth.
claude.howBody: Sign in once, paste your anansi URL into Claude's connector dialog, approve the consent screen that opens in your browser. The exact URL + a copy-pasteable .mcp.json snippet live in Settings → Anansi for Claude.
claude.safety: Anansi is the OAuth authorization server. Tokens are scoped to your account, refresh on a 30-day clock, and revoke instantly from your Claude client.

spider.body1: anansi is named after the West African spider-trickster — keeper of stories, weaver of webs. The mark you've seen throughout this page is Ananse Ntontan, the Adinkra symbol for the spider's web. It stands for wisdom, creativity, and the complexity of life.
spider.body2: The metaphor is structural. anansi is a graph: every goal connects to other goals, to values, to people, to tasks, to the weekly reflection that sits over all of them. Pull on one thread and the others move. The whole point is to see the threads.

coda.body: This is a quiet app. It won't pull at you. It'll be there when you come back.

footer.tagline: A quiet place for goals, relationships, and values. Built for the long arc of a life.
